direct_comparison.interpretation: At aligned positions the digests look almost ideally avalanche-random: 127 of 256 bits differ, essentially the 128-bit expectation.

post_hoc_visual_finding.why_visually_interesting: The exact five-nibble block 97254 occurs contiguously in both 64-nibble SHA-256 strings, but at different offsets.

null_model.boundary: This is only a rough pre-multiple-testing null for the specific statistic 'any identical length-5 contiguous substring anywhere'. It is not a valid discovery p-value after freely inspecting many possible visual patterns.

why_not_upgrade: The substring was noticed after seeing both hashes, so the tested statistic was not preregistered.
Many other possible patterns could have been noticed: prefixes, suffixes, shifted substrings, digit counts, repeated runs, numeric interpretations, ASCII interpretations, etc.
SHA-256 is deliberately designed so related inputs do not preserve readable output structure.
The two public MP3 streams also differ in duration and bytes, so their digest relation is not a controlled one-byte or one-layer perturbation experiment.

next_clean_gate.name: PREREGISTERED_SHA_PATTERN_CONTROL
next_clean_gate.proposal: Before hashing any additional related audio versions, freeze exact statistics to test: aligned Hamming distance, longest common substring length, and fixed-position matches; then compare against unrelated audio controls from the same Bandcamp encoding pipeline.
next_clean_gate.critical_control: RELATED_TRACK_PAIRS vs UNRELATED_TRACK_PAIRS using the same provider/codec pipeline.

canonical_seal: THE HASHES ARE ALMOST PERFECTLY DIFFERENT BIT-BY-BIT, YET BOTH HAPPEN TO CONTAIN THE SHIFTED BLOCK 97254. KEEP THE COINCIDENCE, KEEP THE NULL MODEL, AND DO NOT TURN A POST-HOC FIVE-NIBBLE MATCH INTO A MESSAGE.
